title: The Geologic Time Scale
seo_title: Grade 8 Geologic Time Scale Worksheets: Eras, Relative Dating and Half-Lives
standard_text: Construct a scientific explanation based on evidence from rock strata for how the geologic time scale is used to organize Earth's 4.6-billion-year-old history.
meta_desc: Free middle school science worksheets on the geologic time scale (NGSS MS-ESS1-4): Earth's 4.6-billion-year history, eras and mass extinctions, relative dating from rock layers, half-lives and scaling time to a clock. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Earth's 4.6-billion-year history is read from rock layers.
key_sub: Eras are marked by big changes in fossils. Relative dating orders events; half-lives give ages in years.
body_html:
How to think about it

Earth is about 4.6 billion years old. The geologic time scale organizes this history using evidence from rock layers and fossils.

  • Precambrian (4,600–541 million years ago): early life, mostly single-celled. Paleozoic (541–252): shells, fish, land plants. Mesozoic (252–66): dinosaurs. Cenozoic (66–now): mammals and humans.
  • Era boundaries are marked by mass extinctions, so eras are not equal in length.
  • Relative dating orders events (lower layers are older; a feature that cuts layers is younger). Radiometric dating uses half-lives to give ages in years.
Example

Dinosaurs died out 66 million years ago. Which era ended?

66 = Mesozoic/Cenozoic boundary.

Answer: the Mesozoic

Example

2 half-lives have passed. Fraction left?

½ × ½

Answer: 1/4

Common mistakes

  • Thinking humans appeared early in Earth's history.
  • Thinking an intrusion is older than the rock it cuts.
  • Thinking all eras are the same length.

faq.q: How is the geologic time scale organized?
faq.a: Into eons, eras, periods and epochs, with boundaries at major changes in the fossil record such as mass extinctions.

faq.q: How do scientists know the order of rock layers?
faq.a: In undisturbed rock, lower layers are older; features that cut across layers are younger; index fossils match layers from different places.

faq.q: How long have humans been around compared with Earth?
faq.a: Modern humans appeared about 300,000 years ago, less than 0.01% of Earth's 4.6-billion-year history.
